content:
Thirty-four years ago, Sharon Stone became a sex symbol with her passionate performance in Basic Instinct, and now she says she has embraced being single.

Stone appeared on Mayim Bialik's "Breakdown" podcast this week for a wide-ranging interview, revealing she hasn't been in a relationship for a long time because her romantic life has been "completely fruitless" lately.

The Oscar-nominated actress said: "I've been single for quite a while." She added that she has "reached a point where I really only want to be with someone I like."

Stone's three sons—26-year-old Roan, 21-year-old Laird, and 20-year-old Quinn—have grown up, and she believes her priorities regarding relationships have changed.

She said: "I want to find a partner, not just someone to sleep with. I'm a bit tired of that kind of relationship. So I'm now in a phase of 'completely fruitless,' but I feel this is the stage you have to be willing to reach before you can get what I truly want."

Stone was married to journalist Phil Bronstein for six years, and the two had their eldest son Roan, divorcing in 2004. She was previously married to television and film producer Michael Greenburg from 1984 to 1987.

In 2018, media reports indicated she was dating actor and producer Angelo Boffa, who is of Italian and Swiss descent. The two reportedly broke up later that same year.

Elsewhere in the "Breakdown" interview, Stone said she didn't think she had "experienced the greatest love of her life," and mentioned having spoken with a psychic who told her she would meet her life partner when she was "quite old, almost 70."

The 68-year-old quipped: "That's right now."

Stone is among a growing number of celebrities publicly discussing choosing to live a celibate life. In 2024, musician Lenny Kravitz revealed he had not had sex for nine years, while actress Julia Fox said the Supreme Court's 2022 overturning of abortion rights prompted her to abstain.

In February this year, former Project Runway mentor Tim Gunn, appearing on Chelsea Handler's "Dear Chelsea" podcast, shared that he had been single for 43 years since breaking up with an ex who had been unfaithful back in 1982.

He said this lifestyle prepared him to cope with the extended self-isolation brought by the COVID-19 pandemic in 2020: "I might be one of the few people who truly enjoyed that period."
